notes.title: Charles games turns five! 🎂
notes.content:
Hi! I am truly moved as I write this – more than five years ago, when I joined an informal group of developers at Charles University, I did not imagine myself writing an article to celebrate the fifth birthday of a proper studio that emerged out of it.

Yet, here we are! ⭐️ And since half a decade is not nothing, we have prepared some special things for you. Keep reading and remember: we are where we are in large part thanks to you, for keeping us company all these years. So, thank you from all of us at Charles Games.

To remind ourselves of the journey we've made so far, we created a little video. It is a look back at our humble beginnings as well as our subsequent accomplishments, featuring archive materials as well as commentary by our developers. We hope you like it – yes, you, specifically you, because without you, there would be no us.

Because we are truly grateful to you, our fans, without whom we wouldn’t be able to have made it so far. So, thank you, enjoy, and let’s meet soon. There will be many opportunities to do so in the near future.

[previewyoutube=XTzlud3XaPw;full][/previewyoutube]

The story of Charles Games begins way back in the 2010s, when people from multiple faculties of Charles University gathered to work on serious games. Their passion later made Attentat 1942 happen in 2017 – a game that went on to collect numerous awards, steering the direction of the then-assembling studio. Charles Games was founded in 2020, and Attentat 1942 was there once again, its mobile release being the first title the studio released, along with the next chapter in the form of Svoboda 1945: Liberation.

Since then, we have tried to craft a team and a company that wants something more out of games: to create titles that make an impact, that can be part of the conversation around important topics while remaining engaging. Now, in 2025, it is safe to say that it looks like we have succeeded.

A special occasion calls for special content, and what better way to capture one’s own path than with a timeline? Believe it or not, it also helped us put things in perspective – only after pausing in front of an empty document did we realize that we've done quite a lot over the last five years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/e1e4c9832fd92805b8c7d617e4a42a040de88458.jpg[/img]
([url=https://e.pcloud.link/publink/show?code=XZlT5lZUp1HbFS0yQXbki7o88LvoLBkNUqX&utm_source=charlesgames.beehiiv.com&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=it-s-our-fifth-birthday&_bhlid=e3ee57f6d1509e35903066688d5dfd761ad647de]Click here for the full-size version[/url])

The fact that we’re still here and that we have multiple unannounced projects in the works is a testament to the demand for games about difficult topics, works that utilize interactivity in ways that go beyond entertainment. Not that there’s anything wrong with video games as leisure, but with our creations, we hope to push the whole medium forward at least a little bit. Because, in the end, we truly believe in the power of games to be an expressive medium of the 21st century.

And we can’t wait to show you more of what we’re working on. It’s going to be great, and it will come very soon.

Until then, best regards,
Ondřej

notes.title: Auschwitz liberation 80th anniversary is today
notes.content:
Hello,
on 27 January 1945, Auschwitz concetrantion camp was liberated by allied forces – today, this date also marks the Holocaust Memorial Day. An opportunity to keep remembering the atrocities that happened, in order to not repeat them ever again.

Thank you for playing Attentat 1942 and doing just that. We always wanted to make a difference and seeing people play the game so long after the release is very moving. Thanks to you, we hope to add at least a bit of our own effort to remembering the horrors of the Holocaust.

As a reminder, we put this little snippet of Jakub Hein (who helped your in-game grandfather in Auschwitz) together:
[previewyoutube=Spz64O4-EUg;full][/previewyoutube]
Thank you for being on this journey with us.

Ondřej
Charles Games

notes.title: Official Svoboda 1945 & Attentat 1942 soundtrack is out!
notes.content:
Hello! 
It is with great pleasure that I can announce that our very first Charles Games official soundtrack is out!

The 32-minute album includes a track from both Attentat 1942 and Svoboda 1945: Liberation. Mixing ambient layers with field recordings, experimental as well as historical instruments, it bears an unmistakable touch by its authors DVA. The Czech experimental duo has been around for more than 16 years and it has been an honor to cooperate.

Head to the official Steam page that includes snippets of some of the music - the collection includes previously unheard arrangements!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2009820/Svoboda_1945_Liberation_Soundtrack/

We asked Jan (a half of DVA) about the whole process.

"Creating game soundtracks is a very specific thing. It reminds me of building legos, a lot of loops and emotions you then layer on top of each other. With DVA, we mostly do cheerful music, so Attentat 1942 and Svoboda 1945 have been a big challenge. We had to get serious, dark, which is out of the ordinary."

And apart from innovative voicework, cellos, and folk music, Jan also shares some peculiar instruments used.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/39fd3a3ec654261c2c2fcf02d55d75df31691b70.jpg[/img]
[i]DVA[/i]

"For the most part, we combined field recordings (train station, laundry, water powerplant) and acoustic instruments. We also used a very special bass clarinet, probably used by a German and later Czechoslovak army. Bára, my colleague from DVA, got it in some pawn shop. Even today, you can see the year 1939 on it along with a slightly visible Swastika."

We hope you'll enjoy our soundtrack! If you prefer to get your music on Bandcamp, you can find it on the official page of DVA - https://dva2.bandcamp.com/album/ost-attentat-1942-svoboda-1945-liberation.

And as always, thanks for your continued support!

Ondrej

Imagine you are 20 years old, just starting your university studies. Suddenly, history finds you in your dormitory - how do you act? Will you participate in the demonstrations? Will you manage to flee the Nazi transport headed to a concentration camp? What will you do in the face of evil? Several endings and multiple storylines await.

[previewyoutube=9CSzVbPb0GY;full][/previewyoutube]

The game also includes a virtual museum put together by professional historians. The museum contains testimonies and memories shared by actual witnesses to that chapter in history, along with period documents and photographs. 

We'll be happy if you take a look and decide to leave us your feedback or comment. Together we can make sure that events like these are never forgotten and hopefully never repeated.

Have a great rest of the day,

Ondrej

If you enjoyed Attentat 1942, Svoboda 1945: Liberation won't disappoint you. We pushed ourselves creatively and narratively, bringing you a game that shares the same blood type, while being different in its own way. Check it out here:

Svoboda 1945: Liberation would have never happened without you - our dear Attentat 1942 fans who supported us all these years. So a big thank you is in order. We are happy to start a new chapter of our studio with you.

See you in Svoboda,

notes.title: Today is the 79th anniversary of the attentat on Reinhard Heydrich!
notes.content:
We don't often post about history here, but this anniversary is a big exception. 

If you played Attentat 1942 you know how cruel the Nazi regime was. The ultimate goal of Reinhard Heydrich and other Nazi leaders was to eventually eradicate or assimilate non-germanic nations. 

On May 27, 1942, Josef Gabčík and Jan Kubiš, supported by a vast resistance network, made an assassination attempt on Heydrich. After their weapon jammed, they threw an explosive in the direction of the governor's car.

Heydrich died as a result of the injury days later. Gabčík and Kubiš took their lives, surrounded by Nazis, in a crypt of the Church of Saints Cyril and Methodius in Prague. Today, there's a memorial and a museum you can visit.

The reprisals for Heydrich's death were brutal, including Nazis razing the villages of Lidice and Ležáky to the ground, more than 1500 people were executed, and 3000 Jews were sent to concentration camps.

As you know if you talked to Málek, not everyone agrees about the legacy of the assassination. 

Nevertheless, it is an important event that shaped the history of both Czechia as well as the rest of Europe.

It is a reminder of the immense bravery of those participating in anti-Nazi resistance efforts. Our game couldn't have happened without them. 

Thanks for playing our games, because by doing that, you're helping us to keep those stories and events alive almost eight decades later.

notes.title: Linux is here!
notes.content:
We are happy to bring you another big announcement. We discussed it in previous years, you've been asking us about it, but only after our switch to a new engine (introduced with our previous Remembrance Update) it became feasible. So as of now [b]Attentat 1942 is available to play on Linux![/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/606441bcc4765c61e4a59908d87f157533bb0165.png[/img]

It took some extra programming, video recoding and a lot of testing, but we are really looking forward to seeing what players on another platform will think about our way of approaching World War 2 and history. 

Our mission at Charles Games is to explore the narrative possibilities of videogames, especially when it comes to serious topics. Linux has been something we wanted to do for a long time, to bring our historically-acurate, captivating story to an audience that is keen on playing interesting games. We are happy to erase this debt.

And a final thanks all of you the in comments who helped us to make it happen.

So I hope you'll enjoy Attentat 1942 on Linux! And if you encounter any problems, please let us know here or at info@charlesgames.net.

Ondřej
Community Manager

notes.title: Little patches & Linux coming
notes.content:
Hello!

First of all we're rolling out what is the first post-launch update to Attentat 1942, polishing minor UI inconsistencies and fixing obscure bugs in specific situations. So play now to get the best Attentat 1942 experience on Mac and Windows.

But we also have big news! After weeks of toying with our development tools we reached the decision that we can safely announce that [i]Attentat 1942 will be coming to Linux on June 16th![/i] Rolling out here on Steam as well as other storefronts, with all the features of Remembrance Update. We know that Linux players had to wait, but our recent switch to Unity finally made it happen. And we are really looking forward to seeing the reactions of Linux players! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/285eff8c3cee7509fb2d6a6e300a69015cf5d745.jpg[/img]


[b]We'll be launching the Linux port in the afternoon, at 5 pm UTC+2/CEST. will drop an announcement when it's ready. See you then and take care.[/b]


Ondřej
Community manager

notes.title: Trading cards available!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/735354d30db8a8115bdb81dc4fd8948b021ad182.png[/img]

We just added trading cards you earn while immersed in Attentat's story! We wanted to include them in Remembrance Update from the start, but it took us some time to get all of the requirements right. So instead we decided to postpone to give your the best version of trading cards possible. 

Some of you might have already noticed some of our character portraits popping up in your Steam inventories. There's seven to collect in total. We hope this will improve Attentat 1942 experience for you. 

And thanks for your recent support, we are delighted by all the interest in our game. 

Talk to you again in the future and if you haven't, please check [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1076620/Svoboda_1945/]Svoboda 1945[/url], a follow-up to Attentat, due to be released later this year.

Ondřej
Community manager

notes.title: Remembrance update is live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30943557/184227da79e29e0fc997c477660db484aa13c165.png[/img]

Charles Games could never have happened if it wasn't for Attentat 1942. And our award-winning game just got its biggest update ever. 

We spent a good portion of the last and this year porting the game to a new engine, fixing bugs and improving things as we went. We're excited to show you what is the best version of the game so far, so without further ado, here's what to expect after downloading Attentat 1942 Remembrance Update!

[olist]
[*] Improved UI. New profile screens, new backgrounds for more immersive experience
[*] Steam Cloud save
[*] 64-bit version, meaning [i]Attentat 1942 is available on MacOS Catalina and all near future versions of MacOS to come[/i]
[*] Improved quality of videos and comics. 
[*] Many bugfixes and optimizations
[/olist]

[b]Important thing about the save files[/b]
We tried our best to figure it out, but since we changed engines (letting us to do many more things in future), we are not able to bring your old saves to the new, updated version. But if you do miss them, they are available in the legacy branch in Steam. You can find it all if you right click on Attentat 1942 icon in your Steam library and go to properties>beta branches. Sorry for any trouble this might cause you, but we firmly believe it's worth the hassle.

So that's it and with a mobile port coming soon, the future of Attentat 1942 is bright! And lastly, we wanted to thank you, our players, for your sustained support and feedback. Truly. We never could have done it without you. Thank you for helping us to keep history alive!

From all of us at Charles Games

Ondřej
Community manager

notes.title: Attentat 1945: Remembrance Update is coming, important info about save files!
notes.content:
Dear players,
First of all, thank you for your sustained support and kind words that are still coming, both in reviews and articles. We couldn't go on without you!

The mobile port of Attentat 1942 is coming soon. We had to remake the game from the ground up, switching to another game engine (details in our [url=https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/OndrejTrhon/20190910/350262/From_Air_to_Unity_The_monstrous_cloud_editor_under_our_bed.php]devblog[/url]). This allowed us to polish the desktop version as well and bring you what is the best version of Attentat 1942 ever available! That means not only bringing it to the newest MacOS (Catalina and forwards) but also improving a lot of small things we couldn't do back in the day. 

We decided to call it Attentat 1942: Remembrance update, because we are releasing it the day after the anniversary of the assasination of Reinhard Heydrich was attempted in 1942. The update will, of course, be free for everyone who bought Attentat 1942, thank you again!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/bkgVfbb.jpg[/img]

Most changes were made to the UI. We reworked the look of player profiles, updated character intro screens, improved visual quality of comics and videos. We fixed some bugs hidden here and there and shortened loading times. Under the hood, everything is new!

[b]The update will be coming live at 27th May. We'll be doing a dev stream on our page to celebrate the occasion, we're looking forward to showing you what is the definitive edition of Attentat 1942.[/b]

[h3]So what about the saves?[/h3]
Our switch to a completely new engine means that as much as we tried to figure it out, bringing over save files from the old version will not be possible. We are really sorry for everyone who'll be affected. Upon updating, you'll have to start your game again, albeit keeping all the achievements, of course. But if you are in the middle of a journey to finding your grandpa's fate, you can by all means finish it. We will keep the original game alive in a beta branch, selectable through Steam's settings (we will post the thorough guide later, the option will pop up in Attentat 1942 settings in Steam Library). 

Thank you for understanding. We are excited to bring you a brand new version of our game and we honestly believe it is worth the leap. It also opens up some interesting possibilities for Attentat 1942's future as well, including maybe (psst) Linux version...

So that's it. We are now in the very final phases of testing, tying all the loose ends and preparing everything for what is the biggest update Attentat 1942 ever.

Best Regards and we hope you're safe.

Ondřej
Community Manager
Charles Games

notes.title: Attentat 1942 is coming to mobile and MacOS Catalina!
notes.content:
[i](The picture of Ludmila and Josef was our Valentine's Day celebration contribution)[/i]

It was our goal for a long time, but with switching to Unity engine (we wrote about it [url=https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/OndrejTrhon/20190910/350262/From_Air_to_Unity_The_monstrous_cloud_editor_under_our_bed.php]here[/url]) for Svoboda 1945, a way to finally port Attentat 1942 to mobile opened! ːwinter2019happydogː Both Android and iOS versions are currently in development and if nothing happens the game should be out in spring.

All dialogues and interactive comics' are implemented, most of interactive memories as well. We just need time to test, fine-tune things and make sure the port will be touch-friendly. 

We're looking forward to bringing our historically-accurate game to broader audience. 

[b]Switching engines also means that Attentat 1942 will be again available on MacOS Catalina as we can easily create a 64-bit version! [/b]

In the meantime, consider wishlisting Svoboda 1945, our next effort in making thrilling, yet serious historical games. This time, set amidst postwar chaos:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1076620/Svoboda_1945/

notes.title: Guten Tag! We’re finally available in German(y)!
notes.content:
The wonderful feeling of releasing our game worldwide on Steam had one deep flaw - the fact that our game was unavailable in Germany. USK was not allowed to give age rating to any game containing Nazi symbolism - such as swastikas - that our historically-accurate game contained. This policy has changed only recently and games with such symbolism can now be evaluated. We immediately applied for rating, and are now super proud to finally present Attentat 1942 to our friends in Germany! 

We’re actually the first game released on Steam in Germany containing symbols of Third Reich with the USK rating received after the policy change! 

[h1]German translation[/h1]

Furthermore, we’ve translated the game into German language, so our German-speaking players in Austria and Switzerland, who have been able to access Attentat 1942 in English, can now enjoy the game in their native language along with our new German players!

Thank you for your support!

notes.title: Most AMAZing game Award!
notes.content:
We’re proud to announce that Attentat 1942 has won the MOST AMAZING GAME Award at Berlin’s A MAZE festival! We are absolutely thrilled for receiving the top prize at such a prestigious festival and would like to thank the jury and all our players for your neverending support.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30943557/55f7ce058aedaf6e1e5a60ecbffcb311604c6820.jpg[/img]

Due to German legislation regarding Nazi symbolism in games, Attentat 1942 is still not available in Germany. At A MAZE we've discussed this complex issue and got amazing support from the festival and many individuals including lawyers, who offered to help to release the game in Germany. It will not be an easy process, but we are still determined to do it one way or the other. 

Thanks for the support!
Team Czechoslovakia 38-89

notes.title: The Flare Path: Czechs and Choppers
notes.content:
Real-life boss fights rarely resemble video game ones.

At 10.30 on the morning of May 27, 1942, Reinhard Heydrich, one of Hitler’s most trusted and ardently anti-Semitic lieutenants, was being chauffeured to work through the streets of Prague when a man armed with a Sten submachine gun stepped out in front of his Mercedes convertible as it slowed to negotiate a sharp bend. The cheap SMG refused to fire but shrapnel from an anti-tank grenade thrown by the Sten wielder’s companion pierced the Acting Reich Protector of Bohemia and Moravia in several places causing wounds that led to his death a week later. (more…)
